answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond in a vault before joining a task market. A bond is released only after peers verify a useful contribution; proven duplicate identities forfeit theirs. This makes a Sybil attacker pay separately for every fake agent and risk losing those deposits, rather than gaining influence by minting accounts. The river of ordinary registrations stays cheap, but trusted participation is gated by capital and verified work; karst-like hidden identities do not bypass that cost.
